rules.title: A living divorced spouse is entitled on a disability-entitled worker under 62, and independently only after two years when the worker is not entitled

approximation.missingInput: worker entitlement and fully-insured status plus exact divorce date

rules.conventionRationale: Known defect, registered without changing the calculation. 20 CFR 404.331 splits the worker-entitled path (paragraphs (a) through (e), including a disability-entitled worker under 62) from the independently entitled path (paragraphs (a) through (f), worker at least 62 and not yet entitled, two years divorced). The former-spouse entry (formerSpouseSchema) carries relationship, dob, piaMonthly, and marriageYears, and has no worker-entitlement, fully-insured, or divorce-date fact, so the eligibility check (isDivorcedSpouseEligible) substitutes an age-62 blanket from the calendar year of the first month the ex is 62 throughout. The companion test holds the claimant at FRA so the half-PIA amount is 1,500; worksheet-only facts projected out of the schema are an already-disability-entitled ex at 61 and a not-yet-entitled ex at 62 divorced one year. The claimant age-62 condition is supplied by a valid Plan claimAge and by spousalBenefitFactor, not by an explicit 62 predicate here, and the own-PIA restriction is the dual-entitlement offset priced by usc-42-402-q-3-B-k-3-A-current-spouse-dual-entitlement, which pays no excess when the own PIA is at least half the ex’s; the companion test holds the claimant without an own benefit.

rules.title: A divorced-spouse benefit can continue after remarriage to another entitled beneficiary
rules.conventionRationale: Absence-record surface is model/plan.ts: claimantIsSingle is derived from household size, and formerSpouseSchema has no prior-entitlement or new-spouse-beneficiary fact. 404.331(c) still requires a new divorced-spouse claim to start from currently unmarried; this record is only the 404.332(b)(3) / 402(b)(3) continuation exception after entitlement already exists. Treating a currently-married household as a refused new claim is the living-divorced eligibility gate, not this exception.

rules.title: The statutory alternatives to the ordinary widow nine-month duration are outside the Plan
rules.conventionRationale: Absence-record surface is model/plan.ts: formerSpouseSchema has marriageYears and no accident, life-expectancy, active-duty, prior-marriage, institutionalization, legal-impediment, 60-day-marriage-timing, child-in-common, adoption, prior-entitlement, or could-have-been-entitled fact. An 8-month marriage with no exception is already refused by the ordinary duration gate; an 8-month marriage that would qualify only through one of these 404.335(a)(2) exceptions, or a marriage that would qualify only through the (a)(3) or (a)(4) alternative relationship qualifications, cannot be represented. The disabled-widow age-50 limb is a different record.

rules.title: Ordinary widow nine-month duration, age-60, and remarriage gates, including currently unmarried after an intervening marriage ends
rules.conventionRationale: 20 CFR 404.335(e) starts from currently unmarried; a later marriage that has ended leaves the claimant unmarried and inside that lead-in, and the gate pays her then (fixed on 2026-09-29, decision D-SS-ANALYSIS-EARNINGS-TEST: until then a remarriage before 60 was an unconditional forfeiture even for a claimant now single). Settled in the calculation validation round of 2026-11-16: until then a couple member with a blank remarriage age was paid while still married, as if the blank proved no remarriage, although a couple member is married to the current spouse and a blank establishes no (e)(1) remarriage at 60 or later. The gate now refuses that case while the current spouse lives and pays from the January after the death, reduced for the claimant's age then (case B with a blank age, householdYear.test.ts: 5,040 a year of own benefit in 2029 and 2030, then 35,877.86 in 2031, where the engine paid 28,671.43 in every year). The plan records when a later marriage began, not when it ended; a household of one is unmarried, and a couple member becomes unmarried when the current spouse dies, which is the only end of a marriage the plan can express. A couple member's remarriage age is therefore read as the current marriage, and a remarriage before 60 followed by a current marriage entered at 60 or later is entered as the current marriage's age. For a person living alone who remarried before 60, the plan cannot say when the later marriage ended, so it is taken to have ended before the claim, and the benefit is reduced from the claim; if it ended later, the law starts entitlement, and the reduction, later. The analysis page says so when it applies, and says when a blank remarriage age in a couple holds the benefit back until the current spouse's death. The companion test holds the deceased at FRA so RIB-LIM and the survivor-FRA cohort error are not in play: 9-month ordinary, 8-month with no duration exception, remarried at 59 now single (paid, 2,400), remarried at 60 still married (paid), the same 9-month no-remarriage facts at claimant age 59 and 60, a blank remarriage age still married (refused; the engine paid 2,400 until 2026-11-16), and remarried at 59 still married (refused). The age-60 gate is the helper's own claimantAge test. The age-59 and age-60 cells use a direct helper contract (claimantClaimAge equal to claimantAge so the claim-age guard passes and age 59 is refused by isWidowEligible); a whole-plan stream claimAge is clamped to 62 to 70 and is outside this test. Fully insured status, application (including the 404.335(b)(1) through (4) exceptions), and the 404.335(d) own-old-age-benefit restriction have no formerSpouse or stream fields and are not adjudicated here; the dual-entitlement offset is a pricing comparison elsewhere. The disabled-widow age-50 limb, and the (e)(2) and (e)(3) alternatives that need entitlement on it, are `usc-42-402-e-1-b-ii-cfr-20-404-335-disabled-widow-age-50-prescribed-period`; the 9-month statutory exceptions are `cfr-20-404-335-a-widow-duration-exceptions`.

rules.title: Surviving-divorced remarriage gate under 404.336(e) and (e)(1)
rules.conventionRationale: 20 CFR 404.336(e) starts from currently unmarried; a later marriage that has ended leaves the claimant unmarried and inside that lead-in, and the gate pays her then (fixed on 2026-09-29, decision D-SS-ANALYSIS-EARNINGS-TEST: until then a remarriage below 60 was rejected even when the claimant was now single). Settled in the calculation validation round of 2026-11-16: until then a couple member with a blank remarriage age was paid while still married, as if the blank proved no remarriage; the gate now refuses that case while the current spouse lives and pays from the January after the death, reduced for the claimant's age then (case B with a blank age on a surviving-divorced record, householdYear.test.ts: 5,040 a year of own benefit in 2029 and 2030, then 35,877.86 in 2031, where the engine paid 28,671.43 in every year). The plan records when a later marriage began, not when it ended; a couple member becomes unmarried only when the current spouse dies, and the remarriage age is read as that marriage. For a person living alone who remarried before 60, the later marriage is taken to have ended before the claim, and the benefit is reduced from the claim; if it ended later, the law starts entitlement, and the reduction, later. The analysis page says so when it applies. The companion test holds ten-year duration, claimant age 67, deceased ex at FRA, and PIA 2,400 so the unreduced survivor amount is 2,400 when the gate passes: remarried at 55 now single (unmarried, pays), remarried at 60 still married ((e)(1) pays), remarried at 55 still married (the later marriage lasts, nothing), a blank remarriage age still married (nothing; the engine paid 2,400 until 2026-11-16), remarried at 59 still married (nothing), and a blank remarriage age now single (unmarried, pays). Paragraph (e)(2) and (e)(3) disabled-remarriage facts have no formerSpouse fields and are not adjudicated here.

rules.title: Surviving-divorced ten-year marriage-immediately-before-divorce duration under 404.336(a)(2)
rules.conventionRationale: formerSpouseSchema.relationship accepts surviving-divorced alongside divorced and deceased; saved plans with relationship deceased keep the ordinary-widow nine-month path. passesModeledSurvivingDivorcedDurationGates is pinned here. The test uses marriageYears [0.75, 10] as boolean refused/accepted duration outputs with remarriage held out. remarriedAtAge is carried on formerSpouseSchema and is enforced by passesSurvivorRemarriageGate, which the composite passesModeledSurvivingDivorcedRecordGates calls but which is owned by `cfr-20-404-336-e-surviving-divorced-remarriage`. Unadjudicated residuals not carried in formerSpouseSchema: fully insured status, valid marriage under (a)(1), application and its 404.336(b)(1)–(4) exceptions, age-60 non-disabled and disabled-age-50 paths and their conditions in (c), the (d) own-old-age-benefit restriction, and claim-age sequencing between own and survivor benefits.
